title.en: Factors affecting enzymes, classification and co-factors
title.kn: ಕಿಣ್ವ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಯ ಮೇಲೆ ಪ್ರಭಾವ ಬೀರುವ ಅಂಶಗಳು, ವರ್ಗೀಕರಣ ಮತ್ತು ಸಹಕಾರಕಗಳು

heading.en: Why does fever make us weak?

hook.en: Every enzyme in our body works best near 37 °C and at a particular pH. Shift the temperature or pH and the reactions slow down.
hook.kn: ನಮ್ಮ ದೇಹದ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಕಿಣ್ವವೂ ಸುಮಾರು 37 °C ಮತ್ತು ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ pH ನಲ್ಲಿ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ತಾಪ ಅಥವಾ pH ಬದಲಾದರೆ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಗಳು ನಿಧಾನವಾಗುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: Explain the effects of temperature, pH and substrate concentration.
Name the six classes of enzymes and the three kinds of co-factors.

narration.en: Every enzyme in our body works best near 37 °C and at a particular pH. Shift the temperature or pH and the reactions slow down.
narration.kn: ನಮ್ಮ ದೇಹದ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಕಿಣ್ವವೂ ಸುಮಾರು 37 °C ಮತ್ತು ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ pH ನಲ್ಲಿ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ತಾಪ ಅಥವಾ pH ಬದಲಾದರೆ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಗಳು ನಿಧಾನವಾಗುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Each enzyme shows its highest activity at an optimum temperature and an optimum pH, with activity falling on either side. Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state, while high temperature destroys it because proteins are denatured by heat. As substrate concentration rises, the velocity rises at first and then reaches a maximum, Vmax, which is not exceeded because there are no free enzyme molecules left to bind more substrate. An inhibitor that closely resembles the substrate in molecular structure and competes for the active site is a competitive inhibitor; for example, malonate inhibits succinic dehydrogenase because it resembles the substrate succinate. Such inhibitors are often used to control bacterial pathogens.

points.en: Optimum temperature and pH give maximum activity.
Vmax: all enzyme molecules are busy.
Competitive inhibitor: substrate look-alike that blocks the active site.

narration.kn: ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಕಿಣ್ವಕ್ಕೂ ಅತ್ಯುತ್ತಮ ತಾಪ ಮತ್ತು pH ಇದೆ. ಆಧಾರವಸ್ತುವಿನ ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದಂತೆ ವೇಗ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿ Vmax ತಲುಪುತ್ತದೆ. ಮ್ಯಾಲೊನೇಟ್ ಸಕ್ಸಿನಿಕ್ ಡಿಹೈಡ್ರೋಜಿನೇಸ್‌ನ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಾತ್ಮಕ ಪ್ರತಿಬಂಧಕ.

body.en: Enzymes are divided into six classes: oxidoreductases/dehydrogenases (oxidation–reduction between two substrates), transferases (transfer a group other than hydrogen), hydrolases (hydrolyse ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic and other bonds), lyases (remove groups by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds), isomerases (inter-convert optical, geometric or positional isomers) and ligases (link two compounds, e.g. C–O, C–S, C–N, P–O bonds). Many enzymes need a non-protein co-factor; the protein part is then the apoenzyme. Prosthetic groups are tightly bound (haem in peroxidase and catalase); coenzymes are bound only transiently, and many contain vitamins (NAD and NADP contain niacin); some enzymes need metal ions, such as zinc for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase. Removing the co-factor destroys catalytic activity.

points.en: Six classes: Oxidoreductases, Transferases, Hydrolases, Lyases, Isomerases, Ligases.
Haem: prosthetic group; NAD: coenzyme; Zn²⁺: metal ion of carboxypeptidase.

narration.kn: ಕಿಣ್ವಗಳನ್ನು ಆರು ವರ್ಗಗಳಾಗಿ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಕಿಣ್ವದ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಭಾಗ ಅಪೋಎಂಜೈಮ್. ಸಹಕಾರಕಗಳು ಮೂರು ವಿಧ: ಪ್ರೋಸ್ಥೆಟಿಕ್ ಗುಂಪು, ಸಹಕಿಣ್ವ ಮತ್ತು ಲೋಹದ ಅಯಾನುಗಳು.

problem.en: Classify each enzyme action: (a) a group other than hydrogen moves from one substrate to another; (b) a peptide bond is broken by adding water; (c) two molecules are joined using a C–N bond.

steps.en: (a) Transfer of a group other than hydrogen between substrates: transferase.
(b) Breaking a bond by adding water: hydrolase.
